parameters.query:
-- ============================================
-- LAYER 2: CONTENT-BASED DEDUP (reused from v0.2)
-- ============================================
WITH recent_check AS (
  SELECT 1 FROM app_content_dedup
  WHERE content_key = $1
    -- A message id is stable across the WhatsApp gateway re-deliveries, so it is safe
    -- (and necessary) to look back far. A text hash is not: the same
    -- customer may legitimately send "yes" twice, so it keeps the old
    -- narrow window.
    AND created_at > NOW() - (CASE WHEN $3 = 'id' THEN INTERVAL '6 hours' ELSE INTERVAL '5 seconds' END)
  LIMIT 1
),
insert_row AS (
  INSERT INTO app_content_dedup (content_key, phone)
  SELECT $1, $2
  WHERE NOT EXISTS (SELECT 1 FROM recent_check)
  RETURNING id
)
SELECT id FROM insert_row;

parameters.query:
-- ============================================================
-- Session read + upsert (as-built pattern, db/migrations/001_create_app_bot_sessions.sql)
-- ============================================================
-- Pre-update CTE snapshot: captures updated_at BEFORE the upsert overwrites it,
-- so minutes_inactive is computed off the PREVIOUS activity time, not "now".
-- Do NOT "simplify" this away (CLAUDE.md infra gotchas).
-- ============================================================
WITH existing AS (
  SELECT updated_at AS prev_updated_at,
         current_state AS prev_state,
         current_context AS prev_context
  FROM app_bot_sessions
  WHERE phone = $1
)
INSERT INTO app_bot_sessions (phone, current_state, current_context)
VALUES ($1, 'MAIN_MENU', '{}'::jsonb)
ON CONFLICT (phone) DO UPDATE SET
  updated_at = NOW(),
  -- FIXED 2026-08-13: the 30-minute timeout reset was computed in the
  -- Decision Node but only PERSISTED by paths that happen to end in a
  -- Session Write. The menu-resend path has none, so a stale
  -- QUOTE_COLLECTING row survived and the next message (a digit 4 for FAQ)
  -- was routed by that stale state back into the quote flow carrying
  -- hours-old fields. Applying the same reset here makes the stored row
  -- agree with what the Decision Node already decided, whatever path the
  -- turn takes. The RETURNING block below is unchanged and still reports
  -- the PRE-update snapshot, so minutes_inactive and is_first_contact keep
  -- their exact meaning.
  current_state = CASE
    WHEN (SELECT prev_updated_at FROM existing) < NOW() - INTERVAL '30 minutes'
      THEN 'MAIN_MENU'
    ELSE app_bot_sessions.current_state
  END,
  current_context = CASE
    WHEN (SELECT prev_updated_at FROM existing) < NOW() - INTERVAL '30 minutes'
      THEN jsonb_build_object('menu', app_bot_sessions.current_context->'menu')
    ELSE app_bot_sessions.current_context
  END
RETURNING
  phone,
  (SELECT prev_updated_at FROM existing) IS NULL AS is_first_contact,
  COALESCE((SELECT prev_state   FROM existing), current_state)   AS current_state,
  COALESCE((SELECT prev_context FROM existing), current_context) AS current_context,
  COALESCE(
    EXTRACT(EPOCH FROM (NOW() - (SELECT prev_updated_at FROM existing))) / 60,
    0
  ) AS minutes_inactive;

parameters.query:
-- Record what the bot is about to send, so that when this same message
-- echoes back as a fromMe webhook we recognise it as OURS and don't
-- mistake it for a teammate replying by hand (see db/migrations/002).
-- RETURNING passes phone + text straight through to the send node under
-- both field names the various send nodes use, so this node is a drop-in
-- passthrough that needs no named reference to whatever fed it.
INSERT INTO app_bot_outbound (phone, content_hash)
-- btrim on BOTH the record and lookup sides: the echoed messageBody is
-- trimmed before lookup, so an untrimmed hash here would false-flag any
-- message with edge whitespace as a "human takeover".
VALUES ($1, md5(btrim(COALESCE($2, ''))))
RETURNING phone, $2::text AS message, $2::text AS response;

nodes.name: Record Outbound (Image Reply)
nodes.notes: Passthrough recorder (see db/migrations/002_human_takeover.sql). Left on the default error behaviour ON PURPOSE: it returns the phone + message the next node sends, so swallowing an error here would hand the send node an error object and it would try to message "+undefined". Failing loudly is the safer trade, and Postgres being unreachable already means Session Read failed upstream.

parameters.query:
-- Did WE send this exact text to this number recently? A hit means the
-- bot sent it; no hit means a teammate typed it by hand.
-- 15 minutes is generous on purpose: the echo normally arrives in seconds,
-- and erring long only risks missing a takeover (bot keeps talking, the old
-- behaviour) rather than falsely silencing the bot on its own message.
SELECT 1 AS hit
FROM app_bot_outbound
WHERE phone = $1
  AND content_hash = md5(btrim(COALESCE($2, '')))
  AND created_at > NOW() - INTERVAL '15 minutes'
LIMIT 1;

nodes.name: Lookup Outbound Hash
nodes.notes: onError continues so a DB blip never takes the workflow down. Classify Takeover then sees the error row explicitly and does NOTHING -- an inconclusive lookup must never be read as "a human took over", because that would silence the bot for hours on a live customer.

-- First-touch attribution: the ad that ACQUIRED this lead is never
-- overwritten, because that is what ad spend should be credited against.
-- A repeat click still counts as engagement via touch_count/last_seen.
INSERT INTO app_lead_source (
  phone, conversion_source, source_app, source_id, source_url,
  ad_title, ad_body, ctwa_clid
)
VALUES ($1, $2, $3, $4, $5, $6, $7, $8)
ON CONFLICT (phone) DO UPDATE SET
  touch_count = app_lead_source.touch_count + 1,
  last_seen = NOW();

nodes.name: Record Lead Source
nodes.notes: Terminal branch, fanned out from Is Duplicate? in parallel with Session Read -- attribution can never delay or break a customer reply. Errors are swallowed for the same reason: losing one attribution row is far cheaper than losing a reply. Each query parameter is a single bare lookup, per the n8n comma-splitting gotcha (commas inside the ad COPY are fine; only commas in the template text split parameters).

parameters.query:
-- Is this number already an ACME customer, and have they ever shipped?
-- Phone formats differ between systems (we store 10000000000, auth_user
-- stores 0700000000 / +233 54 968 8677, and sometimes TWO numbers in one
-- field separated by "/"), so both sides are normalised to their last 9
-- digits -- verified against real data 2026-08-14.
-- "Shipped" = an order row exists, per the product owner's Phase 1 definition.
WITH me AS (
  SELECT DISTINCT a.id
  FROM auth_user a,
       LATERAL unnest(string_to_array(COALESCE(a.phone_number, ''), '/')) AS part
  WHERE a.phone_number IS NOT NULL AND a.phone_number <> ''
    AND LENGTH(regexp_replace(part, '[^0-9]', '', 'g')) >= 9
    AND RIGHT(regexp_replace(part, '[^0-9]', '', 'g'), 9) = RIGHT($1, 9)
)
SELECT
  EXISTS (SELECT 1 FROM me) AS is_registered,
  COALESCE((
    SELECT COUNT(*) FROM orders o
    JOIN me ON o.user_id = me.id
    WHERE NOT COALESCE(o.deleted, false)
  ), 0) AS order_count;

nodes.name: Customer Lookup
nodes.notes: READ-ONLY against the logistics app's own tables. Fails OPEN: on error the reply copy falls back to treating the customer as new, which is today's behaviour. auth_user is ~1,850 rows so the un-indexed RIGHT() comparison is a trivial scan today -- if that table grows into the tens of thousands, ask the backend team for an expression index on RIGHT(regexp_replace(phone_number,'[^0-9]','','g'), 9).
